messages:
hana t: Hey all, day 2 here. Trying to get the local stack running on an Apple Silicon Mac. Using Docker Desktop and `docker compose up` (project uses compose v2). Postgres keeps failing during init with a permission error when I bind-mount ./pgdata. Anyone seen this? :confused:

hana t: Logs: 
```
postgres_1  | initdb: could not create directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata": Permission denied
postgres_1  | initdb: removing contents of data directory "/var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata"
```

lev (eng): welcome! :wave: Yep — macOS bind mounts + Postgres + Docker Desktop (especially with gRPC FUSE) can be weird. Quick options: 1) switch to a named docker volume, 2) run a chown inside a container for the mount, or 3) run Postgres natively (Homebrew) and point DATABASE_URL at it. We recommend 1 for reproducibility.

lev (eng): also check whether you launched Docker with the new gRPC FUSE filesystem enabled (Docker Desktop settings). With gRPC FUSE sometimes ownership/perm semantics change; trying the mount with :delegated or :cached sometimes helps for performance but not ownership.

hana t: I tried `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data:delegated` and it still failed. Switched to a named volume `dev_pgdata` and Postgres starts, but my app says connection refused. Postgres logs show it says "listening on unix socket" only.

al (infra): make sure your compose maps the port and uses the same PG envs our repo expects. Example we use in dev compose (compose v2 YAML): 
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    platform: linux/arm64
    volumes:
      - dev_pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: redwood
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: localpass
      POSTGRES_DB: redwood_dev
      PGDATA: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
volumes:
  dev_pgdata: {}
```

al (infra): also note Docker Desktop may pull an amd64 image under emulation; add `platform: linux/arm64` in compose if you want the native arm image.

hana t: added platform and named volume, postgres is up and the app can connect. One annoying bit: our local `scripts/db-reset` runs `dropdb` on the host and fails because it can't access the files in the docker volume (permission denied). Any pattern to avoid touching the volume from host?

lev (eng): we avoid host-level DB CLIs for containerized DBs. Two patterns we use: 1) run psql inside the running postgres container: `docker compose exec postgres psql -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "SELECT 1;"`, or 2) use a short-lived psql container that uses the same network/credentials. Example helper we added: 
```bash
# one-off helper (works from scripts)
docker run --rm --network $(docker compose ls -q) -e PGPASSWORD=localpass postgres:15 psql -h postgres -U redwood -d redwood_dev -c "DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public;"
```

al (infra): if you prefer host postgres for speed, install via Homebrew and set `.env.local` DATABASE_URL to point at it, but note CI expects containerized DB. For people on Apple Silicon who want the best local UX, some folks use Colima which sometimes avoids osxfs quirks.

setup-bot: Internal docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/dev-setup#postgres-local :link: 

hana t: Great — using a named volume + platform flag + running the CLI in-container fixed my workflow. I'll update my onboarding notes and open a tiny docs PR mentioning gRPC FUSE behavior and the :delegated note. Thanks everyone! :tada:
